observations: The conditional design-team router returned no_split; no specialist review adds evidence or changes the primary repair-agent decision.

The executed case_axi_ddr_interface failure is confined to missing current bindings among the board identity document, Vivado export facts, compile-plan authority references, and authorized simulator executables. It is a verification-capability/harness failure; no real board-wrapped simulator execution occurred.

functional_sim and all dependent board gates are not_run or dependency-blocked. Therefore there is presently no admissible board-level claim for numeric correctness, AXI/DDR protocol behavior, data order, liveness, complete DUT weight consumption, lifecycle progress, or output validity.

The historical VCS diagnosis and historical output-frontier symptom are explicitly non-current because live source hashes changed. They may guide instrumentation selection only; they are not current root-cause or lower-layer-contradiction evidence.

Hash-bound operator-leaf and connected single-layer certificates remain reusable. The connected kernel certificate establishes an elastic variable-latency token pipeline with ordered boundaries and cross-token overlap; unequal stage durations are not a defect. No current trace directly contradicts either lower-layer certificate.

The board scope has 16 active same-scope SACG contamination barriers and six open retry requests. Rejected Stage7/Stage8 artifacts remain planning/debug evidence only and block downstream promotion; this candidate repair decision is not a clearance or promotion of those artifacts.
There are no authoritative open backtrack requests in this scoped prompt. A lower-layer replay is not scheduled.

Before the functional replay, the current board harness must bind a complete Transformer-block tensor catalog, immutable checkpoint and stimulus provenance, target-model-generated expected outputs, frozen comparison policy, generated semantic-testbench hashes, and complete-scope DUT weight-consumption requirements. Randomized stimulus is allowed only as input generation, never as expected output generation.

The required weight and golden scope is Transformer blocks only. Embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, sampling, and other model-tail operations must not be inserted into the DUT, DUT weight catalog, or DUT golden boundary.
proposed_actions: Repair only the exact-board simulation authority and semantic-harness binding first; do not modify RTL, lower-layer testbenches, golden outputs, tolerance, checkpoint, stimulus, or board wrapper sources merely to satisfy the checker.

Rerun real_tool.case_axi_ddr_interface immediately after the authority-binding repair. If it does not pass, continue bounded harness/manifest remediation rather than launching VCS or hardware debugging.

After the static gate passes, run the exact-wrapper VCS functional replay with fresh boundary instrumentation and a fresh evidence analyzer. The replay must bind all immutable reference artifacts and report core/ingress/egress/lifecycle observations.

If the fresh replay fails, localize the earliest current board boundary and repair only the named board wrapper, runtime bridge, loader/harness, instrumentation, or compile-plan element. A lower-layer backtrack is conditional on an explicit, hash-bound contradiction to a named lower-layer invariant.

Only after a successful current functional replay, execute the remaining board gate chain and assemble current board semantic evidence. Submit a Stage7 retry only if every required current-layer gate passes and SACG trust barriers are reconciled by the verification result.
risks: Binding a stale identity document, simplified wrapper, unauthorized executable, or stale Vivado export could produce apparently successful simulation that is not evidence for the user-supplied board project.

A missing or replaced target-model reference, changed checkpoint/stimulus, DUT-derived expected output, incomplete tensor catalog, or tolerance change would invalidate functional evidence even if simulation completes.

The current failed static gate must be repaired before requesting a hardware causal trace; treating dependency-skipped VCS output or historical diagnosis as a live trace would bypass the verification contract.

A future output-frontier stall can localize board-wrapper observation points but cannot by itself blame or reopen the connected kernel. Direct hash-bound core start, ingress, egress, named causal-boundary, and current certificate contradiction evidence is required.

Board integration may still expose model/shape packing, numeric representation, data-order, address-map, memory/prefetch, lifecycle, runtime ABI, implementation, or AXI/DDR wrapper defects after the capability gap is closed; no such root cause is established now.
Repeated repair attempts require fresh intervention-response evidence. Reusing rejected reports or changing immutable verification inputs to make a failure disappear is prohibited.
